summary: Well-organized proposal that hits all structural requirements: all required sections present, section lengths within limits, objectives in action form with one-verb phrasing and two-paragraph subsections, two UML figures with informative captions that are both referenced in the text, consistent alpha citation style with citations before full stops, and a 2-3 week iteration schedule that references the objectives. Main problems: the bibliography has only 5 peer-reviewed references instead of the required 6-8 (CRITICAL - easy to fix by adding 2-3 papers on LLM feedback/evaluation and citing them, e.g. in Section 4.3); the schedule's Iteration 1 (08.06.2026) starts 18 days before the stated thesis start date (26.06.2026); and Iteration 9 contains a bare "Documentation" task, which schedules must not include. Smaller issues: three forbidden sentence starters (As/Since/Because), three over-long paragraphs (>10 lines) in Motivation and 4.1, inconsistent naming of the tool ("Reviewer" vs "feedback tool"), and the AI transparency statement does not say which sections of the proposal the tools were used in. All issues are concrete and quickly fixable.

findings.title: Schedule starts before the stated thesis start date
findings.description: The schedule is internally inconsistent with the stated thesis start date. The Schedule section and the title page both give the start date as 26.06.2026, but Iteration 1 is dated 08.06.2026, which is 18 days before the thesis begins. Either the start date or the iteration dates are wrong; correct one of them so that Iteration 1 starts on or after 26.06.2026 (and re-check that the last iteration still ends at the 26.10.2026 submission date).

locations.quote: The Bachelor thesis starts on 26.06.2026 and the submission is on 26.10.2026.

findings.title: Bibliography has only 5 references; at least 6-8 are required
findings.description: The bibliography contains only 5 entries ([TP21], [AAM17], [BBE10], [Bog+07], [NM06]), but the guidelines require at least 6-8 peer-reviewed publications. All five entries are journal articles, so the fix is to add 2-3 more peer-reviewed references relevant to the work, e.g. empirical studies of LLM-based writing feedback or LLM evaluation/benchmarking, and cite them at the appropriate points (e.g. in Section 4.3 for the prompting-technique and model comparison).

findings.title: Schedule includes a documentation task, which is not allowed
findings.description: Iteration 9 contains a bare "Documentation" work item. Schedules must focus on development/research work and should not include documentation-writing tasks, and every item should be a measurable deliverable. Replace it with a concrete, measurable task, e.g. an end-to-end test pass of the feedback workflow in Thesis Management or a usability check with a pilot group.

findings.title: Core pipeline scheduled before guideline input (horizontal split)
findings.description: The schedule splits Objective 1 horizontally: the "core feedback generation pipeline" is implemented in Iteration 2, but the ability to supply custom supervisor guidelines — the primary input of objective 1 ("Generate Feedback Based on Guidelines") — only arrives in Iteration 4, two iterations later. Prefer vertically integrated iterations: in Iteration 2, have the pipeline accept guidelines in some minimal form so each iteration ends with an end-to-end usable feature, and keep Iteration 4 for the full upload/preprocessing workflow.

findings.title: AI transparency statement does not specify which sections the tools were used in
findings.description: The transparency statement names the tools and their purposes, but does not say which sections of the proposal the AI tools were used on. Add a sentence (or short list) mapping tools to the sections they were used in, e.g. which sections were grammar-checked with Grammarly and where ChatGPT/Claude were used for idea expansion, so the statement is specific to this proposal's sections.
